title: Data Sovereignty & Control Plane Brief for Federal Buyers
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Short: a one-stop briefing for sales engineers, AEs, and security champions when engaging federal/regulatory buyers that require strong data-sovereignty guarantees.
- Audience: CISO/CIO, procurement, platform engineering, security architects for regulated agencies and contractors.

Executive TL;DR (for slide 1):
- Redwood Private can run with a customer-owned control plane model so no customer data, telemetry, or audit logs are shipped to Redwood. Only orchestrator metadata (stateless scheduling nonce) optionally flows through encrypted channels and can be disabled.
- We support air-gapped installs, FIPS-certified KMS integrations, HSM attestation, and periodic offline verification bundles for auditors.
- Seller play: lead with minimal-control-plane, show a data-flow proof-of-concept, follow with a compliance checklist (FedRAMP-equivalent mapping), and demo key rotation + offline upgrade flow.

Core message pillars (how to present this to buyers):
1) Customer sovereignty: "You remain the source of truth." Emphasize control over keys, model artifacts, and audit trails. Avoid technical terms like "we host your secrets" — say "customer-managed KMS/HSM integration".
2) Minimal metadata, explicit opt-in telemetry: explain what we need for basic health (capacity tags, instance lifecycle events) and offer a hardened mode that transmits only signed heartbeats.
3) Offline attestability: provide signed upgrade manifests, reproducible build hashes, and an offline audit bundle. Buyers should feel they can validate runtime integrity without contacting Redwood.
4) Operational continuity: canary rollouts, automatic fallback to pinned model variant, and on-prem autoscaling policies — highlight SLA behavior for regional/federal deployments.

Control plane deployment models (short, clear taxonomy to use in demos):
- Fully Customer-Controlled (recommended for high-regulated): Control plane components run in buyer VPC or on-prem; Redwood provides images, manifests, and an operator. No outbound telemetry by default.
- Hybrid Minimal-Control: Control plane control APIs are hosted in a customer-managed network (VPC peering or private link) while Redwood control-plane operators can run outside but with strict mTLS and limited metadata. Good for customers wanting Redwood-managed upgrades but minimal data flow.
- Hosted-Control with Data-Isolation: Redwood hosts the control plane in a dedicated region with contractual data handling restrictions and contractual log minimization. Use only when customer accepts contractual guarantees (lower priority for federal buyers).

Concrete data-flow explanation (language for SEs):
- What never leaves customer boundary: model weights, inference requests/responses, plaintext secrets, PII payloads, audit logs.
- What may leave (in default mode): anonymized uptime metrics (optional), scheduling ephemeral IDs.
- Hardened mode: zero telemetry, signed lifecycle heartbeats only when explicitly enabled by customer.

Common buyer objections and suggested rebuttals (organized by persona):
1) CISO: "How can I be sure you won't exfiltrate secrets or telemetry?"
   - Response: We provide a customer-managed KMS/HSM integration; all keys never leave your cloud/HSM. We run a deterministic installer with signed manifests and provide an offline verification bundle for auditors. In hardened mode we disable telemetry. Offer: run a 2-week POC in isolated VPC with audit hooks.
2) Security architect: "What about supply chain and upgrades?"
   - Response: we publish SLSA-like provenance for our operator images, require image signing, and provide on-prem upgrade packages that can be vetted by your SCA tooling. For highest assurance we support manual (customer-triggered) upgrades.
3) Procurement / Legal: "We need contractual assurances on data retention and deletion."
   - Response: propose a contract clause: "No Redwood access to customer data; Redwood may receive only orchestration metadata if explicitly permitted; logs retained only per customer-configured retention policy." Offer: sample SOW language and redlined template.
4) Platform engineering / SRE: "Will control plane latency/availability affect us?"
   - Response: Our minimal path designs keep hot-path inference within customer boundary; control plane is control-only and does not sit in the inference token path. Show diagram: inference traffic -> local serving runtime -> no egress unless configured.
5) Cost/Finance: "Is this more expensive than hosted?"
   - Response: dedicated/private has higher ops and infra costs; offset by predictable throughput, capacity commitments, and reduced data transfer fees for high-volume regulated workloads. Provide TCO template comparing hosted vs. private for a 12/36 month horizon.

Competitive callouts (short notes for AE/SE to use in live deals):
- MajorCloudAI: previously pitched 'VPC endpoints' but logs/telemetry still flow to cloud control plane; emphasize Redwood's hardened zero-telemetry mode and signed offline verification.
- EdgeServe.co (inference runtimes vendor): strong on edge-device footprints but lacks enterprise-grade control plane packaging + upgrade provenance; Redwood offers signed manifests and a managed operator for secure upgrades.
- In-house build: common pitch — full control at lower license cost. Rebuttal: near-term control may look attractive, but ongoing maintenance, model kernel optimizations, quantization tuning, and continual security patches add ops burden; offer Redwood-managed hardening + SOW for transition support.

Proof points and artifacts to prepare (quick list SEs can attach to emails):
- Signed installer manifests and SBOM extract (example).
- FIPS/KMS integration checklist + sample KMS policy.
- Offline verification bundle: sample audit report and steps.
- TCO workbook for regulated workloads (sheet).
- Two-week isolated POC runbook with checklist and acceptance criteria.

Demo checklist (sales demo flow for sensitive buyers):
1) Start w/ architecture slide: emphasize "inference stays in your boundary"
2) Live: show cluster with control plane disabled telemetry, run an inference request and show network capture confirming no egress.
3) Show KMS key rotation (HSM-backed) and how model artifacts are re-signed.
4) Show offline upgrade: upload signed manifest, run upgrade, produce verification bundle.
5) Walk through compliance mapping: colors for FedRAMP-equivalent controls we touch.

Negotiation levers (what we can offer for federal deals):
- Extended on-site integration assistance (SOW) for air-gapped installs.
- Custom logging retention and deletion SLAs.
- Source code escrow for critical components (limited scope).
- Security carve-outs: allow customer to run a Redwood-run operator image but with customer's CI/CD signing pipeline.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to product & security):
- TODO: prepare hardened-mode test harness (network-capture friendly) and a small script to reproduce demo steps. (Owner: Ajay)
- TODO: formalize contract language for "zero-telemetry" and get legal approval. (Owner: Sofia)
- TODO: create a FedRAMP-equivalent mapping doc (first draft) and attach compliance checklist. (Owner: Daniel)
- Investigate whether we can provide a short automated attest tool that produces a human-readable verification PDF for auditors.

Notes to SEs (quick tactical language to use verbatim):
- "Your data never leaves your cloud unless you explicitly enable telemetry. We integrate with your KMS/HSM so keys never transit Redwood services."
- "We provide signed upgrade manifests and an offline verification bundle so your auditors can validate runtime integrity."
- "If you require air-gap installs we will run an on-site SOW and provide a reproducible install artifact — we can walk your engineers through the verification steps."

Draft email snippet for CISO (short):
Subject: Redwood Private — data sovereignty and control plane options for [ORG]
Hi [Name],
Thanks again for the discussion. In short: Redwood Private offers a customer-controlled deployment model where inference traffic, logs, and keys remain inside your environment. We can run a short isolated POC with hardened telemetry settings and provide a signed verification bundle for your auditors. Attached: demo checklist, signed-manifest sample, and TCO workbook.

Final comments: keep this doc lean; convert to a 1‑page Sell Sheet + 3‑slide demo deck next. Avoid overpromising; map every capability to a concrete artifact (manifest, SBOM, signed bundle).

-- end of draft (notes to self: preserve this as seed for a sell sheet; avoid reusing "controlplane" as a single word in external docs; prefer "control plane" for customer-facing materials).
